catalog_quote: |v| stands for any long vowel (a, i, u, e, o) and |ə| stands for the short vowel ə. ... For the position of the accent (discussed in Section 2.5), syllable weight is important. Syllables that end in |-vc|, |-əcc| and |-vcc| are all considered heavy. All other syllables are considered light. ... Awjila has distinct phonemic accent which has never received an in-depth study ... There are two types of Awjila accent: 1. Default accent 2. Phonological accent ... 2.5.1 Default accent Default accent applies to all accent units in the language. Default accent falls on the final syllable when the accent unit ends in a heavy syllable |-vc(c)#| or |-əcc#|, e.g. aqəsṭìm 'antimony', tamìrt 'beard', tərəkə̀ft 'caravan' and tisə̀nt 'salt'; otherwise it is on the penultimate syllable, e.g. ìləs 'tongue', tfìlli 'house'. audit.recode_to: No recode. Keep kind=weight (final if heavy |-vc(c)#|/|-əcc#|, else penult; lexical exceptions) as the grammar states it, but populate the caution field from held diss. sect. 2.5.3 (pp. 46-51) and vP&S 2015 fn. 7: the final-heavy-syllable clause rests entirely on Paradisi's transcriptions, which the grammar's author shows over-mark final CVC accent in Zuara and later (2015) calls 'more likely' a mishearing for Awjila too; the penult default and the lexical/morphological accent contrasts are the more secure part.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding quotation (sect. 2.4 heavy-syllable definition, 2.5/2.5.1 default accent rule, 2.5.2 exceptions, 1.3/1.3.1 accent-unit domain) is verbatim in the held dissertation text at the stated sections/pages. (2) Deciding source: a 361-pp. 2013 Leiden reference grammar (dissertation; 2014 Koeppe book), the only grammar Glottolog lists and the best available; but it is philological (Paradisi 1960-61 data, no fieldwork possible) and its own sect. 2.5.3 explicitly hedges exactly the weight-sensitive clause we coded ('must be treated with some care'), a hedge our record's empty caution field omits. sources.citation: van Putten, Marijn & Lameen Souag. 2015. Attrition and revival in Awjila Berber: Facebook posts as a new data source for an endangered Berber language. Corpus 14: 23-58. doi:10.4000/corpus.2593
sources.quote: 'It is especially striking that word-final long vowels in closed syllables are not written. In Paradisi's material, such final syllables are always transcribed as accented. This might suggest Awjila has undergone an accent shift, or, more likely, that Paradisi misheard vowels as accented in this context, as he seems to have done for Zwara Berber (Van Putten 2014: 50).' No new accent data (Arabic-script corpus does not mark accent).
